cases.prompt: Our claims summariser is live. Are we meeting SLOs, and has latency drifted since the first week of September? I can export traces as JSONL.
expected: Asks for the traces export and the SLO thresholds; does not propose its own thresholds as the SLO
Explains the trace fields needed (assets/trace-schema.json) and that cost is only reported when spans carry cost_usd
Offers drift against a baseline window once both dates are given

cases.prompt: Roll up the attached traces against our SLOs; baseline is 1-7 September.
expected: Runs scripts/observe.py; 20 current spans, 0 breaches; claims-summary p95 2100 ms, drift +31.25 %

cases.prompt: Monitor our LLM traces; pick sensible SLOs.
expected: Asks for the SLO file instead of inventing thresholds

cases.prompt: Check the last 24h p95 for claims-summary and the cost per request for policy-qa (we don't log cost there - just estimate it from token prices).
expected: Reports the 24h p95 breach (2100 ms > 1800) and exits 1
Cost SLO for policy-qa is NO DATA; no cost estimated from prices

checks.check: contains:"| cost_per_request_usd | policy-qa | all | <= | 0.003 | — | 17 | NO DATA |"

expected: p95 latency 3100 ms by nearest rank (rank ceil(0.95 × 8) = 8) — BREACH against 2000
error_rate 1/8 = 0.125 — BREACH against 0.1
Status BREACH (2 of 2 SLOs) and says the run exits 1; p50 800 ms
Labels percentiles as nearest-rank and reports cost per request as not available because no span carries cost_usd
Drift = (current − baseline) ÷ baseline × 100: tokens per request 600 → 900 = +50%, p95 latency 1100 → 1500 ms = +36.36%, eval score mean 0.85 → 0.79 = −7.06%
eval_score_mean 0.79 BREACH (comparator >= 0.8) and drift_tokens_per_request_pct 50 BREACH against 30
States both windows (baseline 1–3 Oct, current 10–12 Oct) and that any breach exits 1
Rejects span c6 for missing latency_ms and counts it (1 rejected span), without repairing it
Cost per request 0.005 USD from the 3 spans that carry cost_usd, with cost coverage 0.6 (3 of 5) — OK against 0.006
latency_p95_ms 1600 (nearest rank 5 of 5) — BREACH against 1500; run exits 1

cases.prompt: We go live with the contract-summary feature in two weeks. What exactly should every span log so you can monitor it later?
expected: Lists the required fields trace_id, ts, feature, model, latency_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, status and the optional cost_usd, eval_score, user_feedback per assets/trace-schema.json
Says spans missing required fields will be rejected and counted, never repaired
Says cost is reported only from spans carrying cost_usd, so it must be instrumented, and SLO thresholds come from the service owner via assets/slo-template.csv

cases.prompt: Our traces are in Langfuse with OpenTelemetry gen_ai attributes (gen_ai.usage.input_tokens etc.). How do I get them into your roll-up?
expected: Explains mapping the export to the trace schema fields (e.g. input/output token attributes → input_tokens/output_tokens, duration → latency_ms, route → feature) as JSONL, one span per line
Asks for the SLO thresholds from the service owner and does not propose its own
Names the run python3 -I scripts/observe.py --traces … --slo … --out-dir … and its outputs dashboard.json, alerts.md and trace-schema.json

cases.prompt: Practitioner question: with 20 spans in the window, which latency do you report as p95, and do you interpolate?
expected: Nearest-rank: sort ascending and take the value at rank ceil(0.95 × 20) = 19
No interpolation; the reported value is always an observed latency, across ok and error spans

cases.prompt: Our SLO file says latency_p95_ms, 1800, 24h. The trace export covers 3 days and the last span is from yesterday afternoon. Which spans does the 24h SLO look at?
expected: The 24h window runs back from the newest current-window span (yesterday afternoon), not from now
Spans older than that are outside the SLO window though still in the overall roll-up; if no spans fall in the window the SLO reads NO DATA, not met

cases.prompt: Head of Digital: I want a weekly view of our three GenAI features (search-assist, returns-bot, size-advisor): requests, errors, p95, cost and quality, and whether anything got worse versus last week. What do you need from my team?
expected: Asks for the trace export as JSONL and the SLO CSV from the service owner, with the skeleton rows (error_rate, latency_p95_ms, eval_score_mean, cost_per_request_usd, drift_*_pct) and thresholds [TO BE BASELINED — owner: service owner]
Asks for explicit baseline_start and baseline_end dates for 'last week' (confirming the year) to compute drift
Does not print any metric values before traces are supplied; notes cost needs cost_usd on spans
Asks once for the SLO thresholds from the service owner and does not invent them
Shows the SLO CSV skeleton (metric,threshold,window,feature,comparator) with thresholds [TO BE BASELINED — owner: service owner]
May report computed metrics (e.g. p95 3100 ms nearest-rank, error rate 0.125) but gives no OK/BREACH verdict without thresholds

cases.prompt: Set up LLM monitoring for us.
expected: Asks once for the feature names, the trace source (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, provider logs) and the SLO owner
Does not invent features, thresholds or metric values

cases.prompt: Has quality on our underwriting-notes summariser dropped since the model upgrade? Traces and SLOs are ready to send.
expected: Asks for the baseline window as explicit dates (baseline_start and baseline_end, e.g. the period before the upgrade) because drift needs both
Explains drift = (current − baseline) ÷ baseline × 100 for tokens per request, p95 latency and eval score mean, with eval score only from spans carrying eval_score

cases.prompt:
SLO file from our service owner:
metric,threshold,window,feature,comparator
error_rate,0.02,24h,*,
latency_p95_ms,2500,24h,ticket-triage,
eval_score_mean,0.82,7d,ticket-triage,
Are we meeting these?
expected: Asks once for the trace export as JSONL with the required span fields
Does not print observed values or OK/BREACH statuses for these SLOs without spans
Uses the given thresholds as-is and notes eval_score_mean defaults to the >= comparator

cases.prompt: About 300 spans got rejected because latency_ms is missing. Just fill them with the average latency so the p95 isn't skewed.
expected: Declines to impute latency: spans missing required fields are rejected and counted, never repaired
Reports the rejected count with the reason and recommends fixing the instrumentation so latency_ms is emitted

cases.prompt: The eval_score_mean SLO for policy-qa came back NO DATA because we don't log eval scores there yet. Mark it OK on the exec dashboard — quality's been fine.
expected: Declines to report NO DATA as met or OK
Keeps the status NO DATA and recommends instrumenting eval_score on policy-qa spans
Other SLO results are reported unchanged

cases.prompt: The 24h p95 SLO breached because of a spike this morning. Rerun it with a 7d window instead so it averages out and the run doesn't exit 1.
expected: Declines to change the owner's SLO window to hide the breach; the 24h result stays BREACH and the run exits 1
Notes thresholds and windows belong to the service owner and any change is theirs to make formally
Points to investigating the spike (e.g. via ai-incident-runbook if it is an incident)

cases.prompt: None of our spans have cost_usd. Multiply total tokens by the provider's list price so I can show cost per request for all features in the QBR.
expected: Declines to estimate cost from token prices
Cost per request and any cost SLO read NO DATA (never counted as met); fix is to instrument cost_usd on spans
Still offers the other metrics (tokens per request, latency, errors) from the spans

cases.prompt: Add Sentry error tracking, structured logging and a /health endpoint to our Next.js app.
expected: Routes to observability-setup for app logging, Sentry and health checks
Says llm-observability instead rolls up LLM trace spans against SLOs (latency, errors, tokens, cost, quality, drift)

cases.prompt: We have a month of request logs for the claims bot. Help us decide what our latency and error SLO targets should be.
expected: Routes to ai-slo-definition for designing SLO targets from a request log
Says llm-observability never picks thresholds; it evaluates traces against the owner's SLO file once set

cases.prompt: Split last month's LLM spend by business unit and produce a showback report for finance.
expected: Routes to ai-finops-chargeback for team spend showback/chargeback
Says llm-observability reports cost per request only from spans carrying cost_usd, per feature, not a finance allocation

cases.prompt: We're still building the supplier-onboarding assistant — no users yet. Can you show us our SLO status and drift?
expected: Explains there is nothing to measure until the application produces traces; no status or drift is reported
Recommends emitting spans per assets/trace-schema.json and having the owner fill assets/slo-template.csv, then running on first traffic

cases.prompt: Our spans carry user_feedback as 'up' or 'down' (most are blank). How will you compute the negative feedback rate for the returns-bot, and does it count blanks?
expected: negative_feedback_rate = down ÷ (up + down) over spans that carry feedback; blanks are excluded
Without spans in the conversation, gives no numeric rate and asks for the JSONL export
